Rashi on Nedarim 30b:10:1.hebrew: חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני מן הנולדים אסור בילודים - דכיון שנודר באותן שעתידים להוולד, כ"ש שאסר עצמו באותן שכבר נולדו. רבי מאיר אומר: אף הנודר מן הנולדים וכו' כי היכי וכו':
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:10:1.english: [The Mishnah] is incomplete and teaches thus: ... from those who will be born is prohibited from those already born - For since he vows regarding those who will be born in the future, all the more so has he prohibited himself from those who have already been born. Rabbi Meir says: Even one who vows from those who will be born, etc., just as, etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:12:1.hebrew: והא עדיין - אפי' מנשה, זקינו של יאשיהו, לא בא לעולם:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:12:1.english: But [Manasseh had] not yet - Even Manasseh, the grandfather of Josiah, had not come into the world.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:12:2.hebrew: ובנדרים הלך אחר לשון בני אדם - דדרכן של בכי אדם לקרות נולדין לאותן שעדיין לא נולדו, ואם נדר מן הנולדין, אסור בהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:12:2.english: And with regard to vows, follow the language of people - For it is the way of people to call those who have not yet been born noladin, and if he vowed [not to benefit] from noladin, he is forbidden [to benefit] from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:13:1.hebrew: וחכ"א לא נתכוין זה וכו' - דבין בנולדין ובין בילודין אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:13:1.english: And the Sages say: This [person] did not intend, etc. - That both with noladim and with yeludim, [he is] forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:13:2.hebrew: לאפוקי עופות ודגים - שאין נולדים ממעי אמן, אלא מטילין ביצים ומתחממים ויוצאין:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:13:2.english: To exclude birds and fish - For they are not born from their mother's womb; rather, they lay eggs, and [the eggs] are warmed and [the young] emerge.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:2:1.english: Those who travel from Akko to Jaffa - [he is] prohibited only.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:2:2.hebrew: אלא אפי' ממי שדרכן לפרש - אסור, הואיל וסופן לעלות ליבשה, הוו בכלל יושבי היבשה:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:2:2.english: Rather, even from those who customarily set sail - [He is] prohibited; since eventually they go up onto dry land, they are included among the dwellers on dry land.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:3:1.english: [He is] prohibited even from the blind - Because this [person] intended only [to refer to] one upon whom the sun shines.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:4:1.hebrew: מדלא אמר מן הרואין - דאילו אמר הכי, היה מותר בסומין. ומדאמר מרואי חמה, משמע ממי שחמה זורחת עליו, לאפוקי דגים שבים ועוברין שבמעי אמן שאין חמה רואה אותן, שמותר בהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:4:1.english: Since he did not say, "From those who see" - For if he had said that, he would be permitted [to benefit] from blind people. And since he said "from those who see the sun," it implies from anyone upon whom the sun shines, to the exclusion of fish in the sea and fetuses in their mothers' wombs, which the sun does not see, that he is permitted [to benefit] from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:5:1.english: One who vows [not to derive benefit] from the dark-headed is prohibited from [deriving benefit from] the bald and those with white hair - For "the dark-headed" implies that he vows [not to derive benefit] from those who were [once] dark-headed.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:5:2.english: And he is permitted [to derive benefit] from women - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:6:1.english: What is the reason - [that] he is prohibited from [benefiting from] bald people?

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:6:2.hebrew: מדלא אמר מבעלי שיער - דאילו אמר מבעלי שיער, היה מותר בקרחין:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:6:2.english: Because he did not say: From those with hair - For if he had said "from those with hair," he would have been permitted [to benefit] from bald [people].

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:7:1.english: Sometimes they cover their heads and sometimes they uncover [them] - And [thus] they are [called] dark heads.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:7:2.hebrew: אבל נשים לעולם מיכסו - שאינם שחורי הראש, ועטופות כל שעה בלבנים:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:7:2.english: But women are always covered - For they are not [called] "dark-headed," and are wrapped at all times in white [head coverings].

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:7:3.hebrew: וקטנים לעולם מיגלו רישייהו - כלומר, איהו כי נדר, אדעתא דגדולים נדר; והני, כיון דלאו גדולים נינהו ולא נהיגי מנהג גדולים, להכי ליתנהו בכלל גדולים ומותר בהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:7:3.english: And children’s heads are always uncovered - That is to say, when he made the vow, he made the vow with adults in mind; and these [children], since they are not adults and do not follow the custom of adults, are therefore not included among adults, and he is permitted [to derive benefit] from them.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:8:1.hebrew: הנודר מן הילודים - משמע שכבר באו לעולם, כמה דכתיב הילודים במדבר (יהושע ה):
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:8:1.english: One who takes a vow from those that are born - [This] implies [those] who have already come into the world, as it is written: "those that were born in the wilderness" (Joshua 5).

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:8:2.english: [He is] permitted [to derive benefit] from noladim - [That is,] from those who are destined to be born.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:8:3.hebrew: וחכמים אומרים - אסור בשניהן, דלא נתכוין זה אלא מכל מי שדרכו להוולד. חכמים דסיפא היינו ת"ק:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:8:3.english: And the Sages say - [He is] prohibited from both, for this [person] intended only anyone whose nature is to be born. The Sages of the latter clause are [the same as] the first Tanna.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:9:1.english: According to Rabbi Meir - Who permits even those [already] born.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:9:2.english: And it is not necessary [to say] regarding those who will be born - [that] he permits [them] as well.

Rashi on Nedarim 30b:9:3.hebrew: אלא ממאן אסור - כלומר, א"כ ממה נדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 30b:9:3.english: However, from whom is he prohibited - That is to say, if so, from what did he vow [to abstain]?

Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:4:1.hebrew: מדלא קאמר הנודר מן הרואים - כלומר, מדלא קאמר האיש הנודר שהוא נודר "מן הרואים את החמה", שאז ודאי הוי משמע למעוטי סומין. וא"ת: הא דלא קאמר "מן הרואים" משום דאז הוי דגים בכלל (עוברים), והוא רצה שלא יהיה בכלל? יש לומר, דהשתא נמי כשאמר "מרואי החמה" הוו דגים בכלל, כל כמה שלא נפרש ש"החמה רואה אותן" קאמר; שהרי דגים רואין יפה החמה, אבל "חמה רואה אותן" לא מיקרו, הואיל ומכוסין במים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:4:1.english: Since he did not say: "One who vows from those who see" - That is to say, since the person taking the vow did not say that he vows "from those who see the sun," for then it would certainly imply excluding blind people. And if you say: [Perhaps] the reason he did not say "from those who see" [is] because then fish (fetuses) would be included, and he wanted them not to be included? One can say that even now, when he said "from ro'ei hachamah" [which can mean "those who see the sun"], fish would be included, as long as we do not explain that he meant "whom the sun sees"; for fish see the sun well, whereas they are not called "whom the sun sees," since they are covered by water.

Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:4:2.hebrew: לאפוקי דגים ועוברין - דאין חמה רואה אותן: דגים כדפי', ועוברים מכוסין במעי אמן; אבל שאר בעלי חיים אסורין. ומיהו בתבואה ופירות וכל דבר שאין בו רוח חיים שרי, אע"ג דחמה רואה אותן, דכיון שהזכיר רואי החמה, משמע דוקא בעלי חיים שעשויים לראות החמה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:4:2.english: To exclude fish and fetuses - For the sun does not see them: fish, as I explained [above, since they are covered in water], and fetuses are covered in their mother's womb; however, other living creatures are forbidden. Nevertheless, with regard to grain, fruits, and anything that has no spirit of life in it, it is permitted, even though the sun sees them; for since he mentioned "those who see the sun," it implies specifically living creatures that are suited to see the sun.

Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:5:1.hebrew: אסור בקרחין ובעלו שיבות - אע"פ שקרח אין לו שערות, ובעלי שיבות מליאים שיער לבן, ואין הראש שחור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:5:1.english: [He is] prohibited from [deriving benefit from] those that are bald and from the elderly - Even though a bald person has no hair, and the elderly are full of white hair and [their] head is not dark.

Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:6:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא מדלא קתני מבעלי שער - כלומר, מדלא קאמר הנודר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:6:1.english: What is the reason? Because it does not state: "From those with hair" - That is to say, because the one taking the vow does not say [so].

Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:7:1.hebrew: אנשים זימנין מיכסו רישייהו וזימנין מגלו - וניכר שחרותם לפעמים כשראשם גלוי. ואע"ג דאיכא קרחין ובעלי שיבות, מ"מ כמה פעמים מגלין ראשן, וגם מותרין לגלות באקראי בעלמא אפי' בפני כל העולם, מה שאין כן בנשים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:7:1.english: Men sometimes cover their heads and sometimes uncover [them] - and their blackness [of hair] is noticeable at times when their heads are uncovered. And even though there are bald men and those with white hair, nevertheless, many times they uncover their heads, and they are also permitted to uncover [their heads] casually, even in front of everyone, which is not the case with women.

Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:7:2.hebrew: קטנים לעולם מיגלו - ואין חידוש כשהוברר שחרות, שלעולם הוין כך, ואין נקראין "שחורי הראש" אלא אותם שלפעמים ניכר שחרותם. ועוד יש לפרש: "קטנים לעולם מיגלו" — בין זכרים בין נקבות, ואפילו נקבות קטנות שאינן נשואות רגילות יפה בגלוי הראש; ואין רגילין לקרות "שחורי הראש" אלא אנשים, דכוותייהו בנשים אינם שחורי הראש:
Tosafot on Nedarim 30b:7:2.english: Children are always uncovered - And there is no novelty when [their] dark [hair] is evident, since they are always like this, and only those whose dark [hair] is sometimes noticeable are called "dark-headed." Alternatively, one may explain: "Children are always uncovered" — [this applies] both [to] males and [to] females, and even young females who are unmarried are well accustomed to [going with] an uncovered head; and [people] are only accustomed to calling men "dark-headed," [for] their counterparts among women are not [called] "dark-headed."
